chunks: Hadith 5083 — Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man disavows his child after having acknowledged him. He said:
"If the child is from a free woman, the father is to be flogged fifty lashes, the hadd of a slave. But if he is from a slave woman, then there is nothing upon him."

If a man says to another man, "You do the deed of the people of Lūṭ; you have relations with men," he is to be struck with eighty lashes. Likewise, if he says to him, "O maʿfūj, O one penetrated," he is flogged with the hadd of the slanderer: eighty lashes. If a man accuses a group with a single statement, then only one hadd is due upon him if he did not name them individually; but if he named them, then for each man he named there is a hadd upon him. That was narrated by Burayd Al-ʿIjlī from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام.

And it has been narrated: "If they come with him separately, one hadd is administered for each man among them; but if they come with him together, one hadd is administered. If a man accuses another man and is flogged, then returns to accuse him again, then if he says, 'What I said to you is true,' he is not flogged. But if he accuses him of zinā after he has been flogged, then the hadd is upon him. And if he accuses him ten times before he is flogged, there is only one hadd upon him."

key_terms.حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ: the legal punishment prescribed for one who makes a slanderous sexual accusation
key_terms.حُرَّةٍ: a free woman, as opposed to a bondwoman

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for slander, denying acknowledged paternity, and repeated accusations in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning denial of paternity after prior acknowledgment and the hadd of slanderous accusation. It also details how punishment is applied in cases of accusing individuals or groups, and whether repeated accusations incur one or multiple legal punishments depending on circumstance.
